newsitem.title: USA: McDermott, subsidary open probes, predict losses.
newsitem.headline: McDermott, subsidary open probes, predict losses.

text.p: Energy services firm McDermott International Inc. said Monday it and its majority-owned offshore contruction subsidiary, J. Ray McDermott S.A., have begun a probe into unspecified allegations of wrongdoing at the companies.

McDermott International also said it expected to report a loss of as much as $200 million for its fiscal fourth quarter after charges of $130 million for uninsured asbestos claims and write-downs on various assets. McDermott said the losses and the investigation were not related.
The undisclosed allegations, which involved several unnamed former employees of both companies, could lead to civil and criminal penalties if proven true, McDermott said in a statement.
"The companies have begun an internal investigation into these allegations and have engaged outside legal counsel to assist them in conducting such investigation," McDermott said.
The companies declined further comment, and trading in their stock was halted for the day at their request.

"I will have no comment on the allegations of wrongdoing," said Chief Executive Officer Roger Tetrault, a former General Dynamics Corp. executive brought on board in March to begin turning the ailing New Orleans-based company around.
Separately, McDermott International said fiscal fourth quarter losses for it and its J. Ray McDermott subsidiary will be significantly bigger than in the same quarter last year.

J. Ray McDermott expects to report a $60 million to $70 million net loss for the quarter, compared with a loss of $17.4 million, or 50 cents a share, a year ago. The company's earnings were hurt by lower offshore barge income in the Gulf of Mexico and Far East and unrealized currency exchange losses in a foreign joint venture, it said.

McDermott International expects to report a $180 million to $200 million net loss for the quarter, compared with a loss of $3.9 million, or 11 cents a share, a year earlier. The loss includes the write-down, revised terms on international power generation contracts and continuing losses in its engineering, construction and shipbuilding operations, it said.

"Their backlog still has some bad-margin business in it, and just in general you hate to see continuing write-downs. But hopefully this is the housecleaning write down," Simmons and Co. International analyst Roger Read said.

McDermott International said it plans to sell or write off non-core assets and focus on its core marine construction, power generation and government contracting businesses as it restructures operations, Tetrault said.

The company also expects to slash its general and administrative costs in part by cutting 95 of its 400 headquarters jobs and ending sponsorship of the New Orleans stop on the Professional Golf Association tour, Tetrault said.
"At a minimum, I expect we will be profitable in fiscal 1998," Tetrault said on a conference call with analysts.
McDermott International stock was halted at $21 and J. Ray McDermott stock was halted at $22.50, both on the New York Stock Exchange.
McDermott International is a worldwide energy services company and majority owner of offshore construction firm J. Ray McDermott, also based in New Orleans.
